market.label: Bearish
market.advice: Nifty is below its 200-day average. Strategies make no new buys in this regime (protects capital) and only manage existing positions.

strategies.name: Momentum leaders
strategies.description: Holds the 15 strongest stocks by risk-adjusted 6- and 12-month return (the method behind NSE's Nifty200 Momentum 30 index), reviewed monthly; a holding is kept while it stays in the top 30. Momentum is the most consistently documented stock-selection effect worldwide and in India (IIM-A factor data: ~10%/yr long-short since 1994). Crashes hard in sharp reversals (2008-09).
strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

strategies.name: Earnings gap-up (PEAD)
strategies.description: Post-earnings-announcement drift: after quarterly results, a stock that gaps up 4%+ on 3x volume and holds the gap tends to keep rising for weeks (Ball & Brown 1968; mixed but positive Indian evidence). Results dates from NSE's event calendar. 8% stop, 40-day holding limit, exit on a close below the 50-day average.
strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

strategies.name: Nifty trend timing (ETF)
strategies.description: Holds the NIFTYBEES index ETF while Nifty is above its 200-day average and moves to cash when it falls below (checked monthly). Faber's market-timing rule: similar long-run return to buy-and-hold with much smaller crashes; whipsaws in sideways markets.
strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

strategies.name: Golden cross trend
strategies.description: Buys when the 50-day average crosses above the 200-day average (a 'golden cross') in a strong stock, and holds until the 'death cross' (50-day back below 200-day). Classic long-term trend following; slow, many small losses, a few big winners.
strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

strategies.name: Volatility contraction (VCP) breakout
strategies.description: A leader near its 52-week high goes quiet - a tight 15-day box (under 12% high-to-low) with shrinking volatility - then breaks out of the box on 1.5x volume (Minervini's VCP / Darvas box). Stop 7%, exit on a close below the 50-day average.
strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

strategies.name: Trend-template breakout
strategies.description: Minervini SEPA-style: a stock in a strong uptrend (above rising 50/150/200-day averages, near its high, relative strength in the top 10%) breaking its 20-day high on 2x volume. 8% stop, exit on a close below the 50-day average. Out of sample it only matched the average stock.
strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

strategies.name: Dual momentum (ETF rotation)
strategies.description: Each month holds the 2 ETFs with the best 12-month return among Nifty, Nifty Next 50, Bank, Gold and Nasdaq-100 - but only if that return is positive, otherwise cash (Antonacci's dual momentum: relative + absolute momentum across asset classes).
strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.

strategies.name: Sector rotation
strategies.description: Each month finds the 3 strongest industries (average 6-month return of their stocks) and holds the strongest stocks inside them. Industry momentum is documented (Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999) and partly explains stock momentum.
strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.

strategies.name: Turtle / Donchian 55-day breakout
strategies.description: The Turtle Traders' System 2: buy a new 55-day high, exit on a new 20-day low, with a 2-ATR initial stop. Only stocks above their 200-day average. Trend following has strong evidence in futures; on single stocks it is weaker and whipsaws in sideways markets.
strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.

strategies.name: Bollinger squeeze breakout
strategies.description: When Bollinger Bands are at their narrowest in 6 months (a volatility squeeze) and price closes above the upper band in an uptrend, volatility tends to expand in that direction. Exit on a close below the 20-day average; 8% stop.
strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.

strategies.name: Pullback in leaders (21-EMA)
strategies.description: Buys a relative-strength leader (RS 80+) in a stage-2 uptrend when it pulls back to its 21-day EMA and bounces (low touches the EMA, close above it). Exit: close below the 50-day average or after 20 days; 7% stop. 'Buy the dip in strong stocks'.
strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.

strategies.name: NR7 breakout
strategies.description: Toby Crabel's narrow-range pattern: after the quietest day in 7 sessions, a close above that day's high in an uptrending leader. Short holding (exit below the 10-day average or after 7 days), 5% stop.
strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.

strategies.name: Low volatility
strategies.description: Holds the 20 steadiest large, liquid stocks (lowest 1-year volatility), reviewed quarterly - the method behind NSE's Nifty100 Low Vol 30 index (17.7% vs 13.7%/yr for Nifty 100, 2005-18, and much smaller crash losses). Defensive: lags in strong rallies.
strategies.status_reason: Did worse than Nifty / the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.

rejected_strategies.name: RSI-2 pullback (Connors)
rejected_strategies.description: Larry Connors' short-term mean reversion: buy a 1-3 day plunge (RSI-2 under 10) in a stock above its 200-day average, sell on the bounce. Works in US large caps; here it lost money after realistic costs (reversal mostly works in illiquid stocks).
rejected_strategies.status_reason: Beat the market in one recent window but not the other.
rejected_strategies.rejected_reason: Lost money after realistic Indian delivery costs (short-term reversal works mostly in illiquid stocks).

rejected_strategies.name: Near 52-week high
rejected_strategies.description: Holds uptrending stocks trading closest to their 52-week high (George & Hwang 2004). In our tests it never beat the average stock.
rejected_strategies.status_reason: Beat both Nifty and the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.
rejected_strategies.rejected_reason: Never beat the average stock in our tests.

rejected_strategies.name: Old textbook rules (baseline)
rejected_strategies.description: The v1 rules (50-DMA volume breakout, 52-week-high breakout) with 5% stop / 10% target / 15 days. Kept only as a 'what not to do' comparison (-12%/yr in testing).
rejected_strategies.status_reason: Did worse than Nifty / the average stock over the last 12 and 6 months.
